newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian construction industry in tailspin.
newsitem.headline: Colombian construction industry in tailspin.

text.p: New cement orders dropped 12 percent in the first half of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995 as Colombia's construction industry continued to be hit by negative growth, the National Statistics Department (DANE) said.

It said cement orders during the six-month period totalled just 3.65 million metric tons, down sharply from previous years when the construction industry was one of Colombia's most dynamic and profitable.
In June 1996, new cement orders totalled 558,900 metric tons, down 19.70 percent from June 1995.
Issuance of new construction permits fell 26.70 percent during the first half of 1996 from the same period last year, the DANE said.

It added that number of new loans approved by Colombian savings and loans -- a mirror of conditions in the construction industry -- fell 12.99 percent during the six-month period from January-June 1995.

The slowdown in construction began in early 1995 when high domestic interest rates and a crackdown on the Cali drug cartel began affecting growth. The cartel laundered huge sums of narcotics money through building projects in the capital and elsewhere.
